stem_book: A car, starting from rest, accelerates at the rate f through a distance S, then continues at constant speed for time t and then decelerates at the rate f/2 to come to rest. If the total distance traversed is 15S, then: (a) S = (1/2)ft² (b) S = (1/4)ft² (c) S = ft (d) S = (1/72)ft²
work: v² = 2fS; braking distance = v²/(2·f/2) = 2S ⇒ cruise = 15S − S − 2S = 12S = √(2fS)·t ⇒ 144S² = 2fSt² ⇒ S = ft²/72
